resources.string: Apex
Pump driver for the Apex TruCare III insulin pump (Bluetooth).
Apex: the driver is not ready yet.

No Bluetooth password is entered in AAPS, so the driver is not working with the pump. Connect the pump on the Apex pump connection screen: its serial, then the current B/P from the pump status screen; for a pump with its password switched off, enter 000000.
The phone\'s Bluetooth is off. The driver does not connect to the pump until it is on.
The pump refused the Bluetooth password ten times, so the driver has stopped trying. Read the current B/P from the pump status screen and enter it in the Apex settings.
The pump refused the Bluetooth password. Read the current B/P from the pump status screen and enter it again.
Apex pump connection

1. Enter the eight digit serial number printed on the pump and press Find. Only the pump with this serial is looked for: no other pump nearby can be connected by mistake.\n2. Once the pump is found, enter its Bluetooth password, the six digits shown as B/P on the pump status screen.\n3. Press Connect. The serial and the password are kept only if the pump answers.

Write the driver trace
One line per event in the AAPS log, for measuring how often the pump is contacted and in what order things happen
Keep the pump connection open

Stay connected between exchanges instead of reconnecting every few minutes. The pump sends a signal every few minutes, and the connection is dropped and rebuilt if that stops arriving. Turn this off only if the connection proves unreliable on this phone.
2. Bluetooth password (B/P on the pump screen), 6 digits
1. Serial number (on the pump case), 8 digits

Disconnect

Removes what the connection needs: the serial number, the password and the Bluetooth address of the pump. The driver also forgets what it knew of the pump: its status, battery, profiles and the last comparison of the day. The copies of the pump journals in the driver\'s database and the treatments in AAPS stay.
Change the pump password
Sets a new random password for the connection with the pump. The new password is shown on the pump status screen as B/P.

Apex: the pump refused the command.
Apex: no reconciliation before the command: the pump did not answer, or a bolus runs. The command was not sent.

Apex: the firmware version of the pump could not be read. Without it the driver does not know how to read the pump\'s records: nothing is checked and no command is sent until it is read. It asks again at the next connection.
Apex: the driver cannot settle the pump journal: an error in the driver. Boluses of the loop are stopped until it can. Send the AAPS log to the developer.
Apex: the driver could not reconcile with the pump since AAPS started, %1$d tries in a row. Boluses of the loop are not given until it can. Check the pump and its connection.

Apex: the pump gave no usable answer to three requests in a row. Nothing more is sent to it until it answers again: its heartbeat, the next command of the loop or a new connection. Check the pump and its connection.
Apex: the pump did not take the bolus. Check the pump and its connection.
Apex: the pump delivered %1$.3f U of the %2$.3f U asked for.
Apex: the pump is stopped, has an alarm or is locked, so it takes no commands. Check the pump.
Apex: the pump speaks protocol %1$s, older than 4.10. Such a pump gives no daily statistics, and the driver does not work without them: no command is sent to the pump and nothing is written to AAPS.
Apex: the pump wrote a faulty record of the bolus at %1$s. %2$.3f U is written, as the count kept by the pump gives it. Check the bolus in the treatments.
Apex: the pump reported a bolus of %2$.3f U at %1$s, more than its reservoir held. Its memory may be at fault. Nothing is written. Check the pump and the treatments.
Error in settling the pump journal: the data from %1$s to %2$s differ by %3$.3f U. IOB may be wrong. The loop is open.

Second error in settling the pump journal today: the data from %1$s to %2$s differ by %3$.3f U. IOB may be wrong. The loop is open. This is a serious error of the driver: tell the developer and send the AAPS log.
Apex: the pump journal has more than one faulty record of one day. %2$.3f U they hold together is written at %1$s, to the first of them. Check the treatments.
Apex: reconciliation with the pump: the pump wrote no record of the bolus of the loop at %1$s. By its own count it delivered %2$.3f U, and that is written. Check the bolus in the treatments.
Apex: the pump did not write the record of a bolus at %1$s, and the count kept by the pump does not tell its amount. Nothing is written. Check the treatments.
Insulin change by refill
When the reservoir grows by 5 U or more, an insulin change is written to the careportal.
A refill on the pump is not written. Record the insulin change in AAPS yourself.
